chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from 'Abd Allah ibn Bah'r from a man from Zurarah, who said:
I asked: 'The fish leaps from the water and falls onto the bank, and wriggles until it dies.' He said: 'Eat all of it.'

The meaning in this report is that we interpret it as: when it came out of the water, he caught it while it was alive, then it died; its eating is permissible. But if it died before he caught it, eating it would not be permissible. This indicates that.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat fish that die on land after leaping out of water?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between fish that die in water (ma'khum) and those that leap out alive, establishing that the latter remain permissible (ja'iz) as long as they are caught while still living. The scholar highlights that the permissibility hinges on the moment of capture rather than the location of death, reflecting the Shia principle that fish are generally exempt from the requirement of ritual slaughter (dhikr) provided they are not explicitly prohibited species.
